items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: On board I met the leader of a Cuban orchestra... He was a violinist named Bernardo Alemany.

ctx.x: Joe Hayman, Herman Chittison, Fletcher Allen, Burns and myself. We contacted "Spider" Courance who was still working at the Villa d'Este and Burns knew a drummer from Holland who was a Negro born in the Dutch West Indies. His name was Arthur Pay. Pastraudis said that there was an Italian bass player already in Alexandria.

We left Paris by train for Italy the 5th of December 1938 without telling anything to anybody and sailed from Genoa the following day, on the Italian liner Esperia. On board I met the leader of a Cuban orchestra whom Pastraudis had engaged as an Argentina Orchestra. He was a violinist named Bernardo Alemany. We had a wonderful trip but when we arrived at Alexandria we could not leave the boat because Pastraudis did not have the working permits for us. But he was a big man in Alexandria and he told us that he…

Before leaving Paris I gave Mae enough money for Beezie and Joan to go back to New York. Mae was coming to Egypt after "Spider" got settled there. She told me that Beezie was out of town, staying for a few days with a sick friend.
